Introducing Yourself in German: A1 Phrase Practice

Practise names, origin and a short introduction in German. Use heißen, kommen and vorstellen with translated models and explained exercises.

A1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Useful phrases and patterns

A short introduction can give your name, origin and role. Use Ich heiße … for a name, Ich komme aus … for origin and Ich bin … for a role. In a formal setting, Darf ich mich kurz vorstellen? politely opens the introduction. Share only the information relevant to the conversation.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not confuse a name with age: Ich heiße names you, while Ich bin … Jahre alt gives your age. Keep the sentence pattern linked to its purpose.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich heiße Leena und bin neu in der Gruppe.My name is Leena and I am new to the group.
Worked example 2Ich komme aus Pune und wohne jetzt in Leipzig.I come from Pune and now live in Leipzig.
Worked example 3Darf ich mich kurz vorstellen? Mein Name ist Jonas Berg.May I briefly introduce myself? My name is Jonas Berg.
Worked example 4Ich bin Auszubildende in einer Bäckerei.I am a trainee at a bakery.

Practice: complete the phrases

Complete the introduction using the verb or meaning cue in brackets. Use the present tense unless an infinitive is requested. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Word bank: aus · heiße · ist · vorstellen

Question 1. Ich ___ Nils und arbeite hier im Team. (heißen)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: heiße

Ich heiße is the name pattern; ich takes heiße.

Question 2. Ich komme ___ Spanien. (origin preposition)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: aus

Aus introduces origin in this country expression.

Question 3. Darf ich mich kurz ___? (vorstellen, infinitive)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: vorstellen

After darf, the reflexive introduction uses the bare infinitive vorstellen.

Question 4. Mein Name ___ Amira. (sein)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: ist

The subject Mein Name is singular, so use ist.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
